newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria buys EU soft wheat flour - traders.
newsitem.headline: Algeria buys EU soft wheat flour - traders.

text.p: Algeria recently made a large purchase of European Union soft wheat flour at $305 per tonne, including cost and freight, European grain traders said on Wednesday.
One trader said Algeria bought 130,000 tonnes of EU wheat flour for September shipment but others operator had no details on tonnages involved.
The flour was expected to come from Italy, Spain, and possibly the Netherlands, they said.
French millers, traditionally large suppliers of flour to Algeria, said the price of the transaction was "extremely low" even if Italy and Spain enjoy a freight advantage on that destination.
Italy now tops the list of Algeria's wheat flour suppliers, a position France has lost partly due to the high cost of its Coface export credit insurance on that destination.

Between July 1 and August 20 the European Union granted licences to export 621,791 tonnes of EU flour to non-EU countries, including 219,120 tonnes in France, 135,232 tonnes in Spain, and 42,043 tonnes in the Netherlands.
Prefixing of licences for daily EU wheat flour exports was reestablished on July 25.
